gloss: June (traditional name); a type of wagashi

definitions.explanation: The old Japanese name for the sixth month. Despite the characters literally suggesting 'month without water,' it actually refers to the month when rice paddies are filled with water ({水|みず}の{月|つき}). Still used in literary, poetic, and cultural contexts.

definitions.gloss: a triangular wagashi (Japanese sweet) eaten on June 30
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese confection made of sweetened rice flour topped with sweet azuki beans. It has a distinctive triangular shape representing ice. Eaten on June 30 as part of the Nagoshi no Harae purification ritual to ward off illness for the rest of the year.

examples.japanese: {水無月|みなづき}は{梅雨|つゆ}の{季節|きせつ}だ。
{旧暦|きゅうれき}では{六月|ろくがつ}を{水無月|みなづき}と{呼|よ}ぶ。
examples.english: In the old calendar, June is called Minazuki.

examples.japanese: {水無月|みなづき}の{風|かぜ}が{心地|ここち}よい。
examples.english: The breeze in June feels pleasant.

examples.japanese: {六月|ろくがつ}になると{和菓子屋|わがしや}に{水無月|みなづき}が{並|なら}ぶ。
examples.english: When June comes, minazuki sweets appear in wagashi shops.

examples.japanese: {三角形|さんかくけい}の{水無月|みなづき}は{氷|こおり}を{表|あらわ}している。
examples.english: The triangular shape of minazuki represents ice.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}では{六月|ろくがつ}{三十日|さんじゅうにち}に{水無月|みなづき}を{食|た}べる{習慣|しゅうかん}がある。
examples.english: In Kyoto, there is a custom of eating minazuki on June 30.

notes:
One of the twelve traditional Japanese month names ({和風月名|わふうげつめい}). The characters {水|みず}{無|な}{月|つき} literally mean "month without water," but this is interpreted as {水|みず}の{月|つき} (month of water), referring to the flooding of rice paddies during the rainy season.

TRADITIONAL MONTH NAMES:
- {睦月|むつき} (January), {如月|きさらぎ} (February), {弥生|やよい} (March)
- {卯月|うづき} (April), {皐月|さつき} (May), {水無月|みなづき} (June)
- {文月|ふみづき} (July), {葉月|はづき} (August), {長月|ながつき} (September)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {水無月|みなづき} sweet (sense 2) is especially associated with {京都|きょうと}. It is eaten on June 30 during {夏越|なごし}の{祓|はら}え, a Shinto purification ritual held at the midpoint of the year. The triangular shape symbolizes ice, which was a luxury in ancient times, and eating it was believed to ward off summer illness.
